name: Christian
headline: Turn Lufthansa’s booking data into customers who stay.
saw: Across a customer base as broad as yours, business travellers, holiday flyers and long haul passengers are usually reached with the same offers and messages, whatever the way they fly.

Once someone has booked, the signal you already own is what they fly, how far ahead they book, which cabin they choose and when they rebook or cancel. Today that signal sits in analytics, not in the message the customer receives.

Cross-sell, upsell and retention campaigns are typically built by hand, per segment, per month. The passenger who is about to book with another carrier this week gets the same offer as everyone else, or none at all.
help_intro: Three places where an AI that decides per customer, not per segment, pays for itself in the first quarter.

cases.head: Stop the switch before it happens
cases.text: Per traveller signals from booking patterns, cancellations and rebookings show who is about to fly another carrier. The right offer, channel and moment, picked for each one.
cases.kpi_label: lower churn, measured at Flytxt telecom clients

cases.head: Offer the next trip that fits
cases.text: Next best offer per traveller, based on routes flown, cabin choices and trip frequency. Upgrades and add-ons go to people who want them, not to everyone on the list.
cases.kpi_label: category subscriptions at an OTT client

cases.head: Keep every traveller engaged between trips
cases.text: Travel content and offer nudges through email and messages, so each traveller has a reason to book again. Timed to their travel pattern, not the calendar of a campaign team.
cases.kpi_label: streaming activity at an OTT client
